kept.title: Insufficient DNS Rebinding Mitigation
kept.description: The logic in src/helpers.ts uses a race-prone, non-authoritative DNS resolution process (resolve_all_records) which is vulnerable to DNS Rebinding attacks where the attacker serves an internal IP after the initial validation check.
steps_to_exploit: Attacker sets up a malicious domain
First request returns a public IP
Attacker changes DNS record to 127.0.0.1
The library performs second resolution too late or with insufficient entropy to prevent the state switch
kept.impact: Allows attackers to bypass SSRF protection and access internal services/metadata endpoints.

kept.title: Incomplete Blacklist for SSRF Protection
kept.description: The BAD_RANGE_USED_IN_SSRF list in src/helpers.ts is a hardcoded blacklist rather than a whitelist or a robust network-layer filter, failing to cover all private/link-local address spaces (e.g., IPv6 ULA or specific link-local ranges).
steps_to_exploit: Identify an internal network address not in the hardcoded list
Craft a URL using that address
Library fails to identify it as internal due to missing range definitions
kept.impact: Direct bypass of SSRF security controls allowing access to internal infrastructure.

kept.title: Unsafe URL Protocol Validation
kept.description: The is_proto_safe function only performs regex-based string matching, failing to consider complex URI schemes or edge cases that might be interpreted differently by lower-level libraries or underlying Node.js modules.
steps_to_exploit: Submit a URL with a malformed protocol (e.g., 'http://', 'javascript:'),
Bypass regex with non-standard characters
Trigger code execution in downstream sinks
kept.impact: Potential for protocol smuggling or bypass of expected scheme restrictions.

kept.title: Potential Command/Code Injection via Unsanitized Regex
kept.description: The regex used in replace_two_slashes_url_to_normal_url is vulnerable to ReDoS (Regular Expression Denial of Service) and processes input without length limits.
steps_to_exploit: Craft a long, repetitive string input
Submit to the function
Observe increased CPU usage leading to process hang
kept.impact: Denial of Service of the security utility library.

kept.title: Reliance on Loose URI Parsing
kept.description: The library uses the global URL constructor for validation, which is known for inconsistent behavior across different Node.js versions and environments regarding edge cases like empty hostnames or backslashes.
steps_to_exploit: Provide a URL like 'http://[::1]' or encoded variants
Library might normalize it differently than the underlying HTTP client (got)
Request is sent to an internal host unexpectedly
kept.impact: Security bypass due to parser differential/discrepancy.

kept.title: Hardcoded Secret Risk in CI
kept.description: The codebase contains references to multiple tokens like LABELER_TOKEN and SNYK_TOKEN, implying management of sensitive secrets within the repository configuration files.
steps_to_exploit: Compromise the repo
Access GitHub Action secrets variables
Use tokens to escalate privileges in Snyk or GitHub
kept.impact: Unauthorized access to CI/CD pipelines and external security tooling.

kept.title: Insecure Use of 'got' Dependency
kept.description: The library uses 'got' to perform HEAD requests for redirect validation without robustly configuring the Agent or explicitly disabling internal network access for the fetcher itself.
steps_to_exploit: Redirect to an internal metadata IP (e.g., 169.254.169.254)
The validation library might accept the initial check but the fetcher reaches the endpoint
kept.impact: SSRF vulnerability during the redirect handling process.

kept.title: Insecure Default Cron Configuration
kept.description: The njsscan workflow is configured to run every minute, which is excessive and could lead to unnecessary resource consumption or API rate-limiting issues.
steps_to_exploit: Monitor CI/CD throughput
Observe high frequency of automated scans
Potential for exhausting repository action minutes
kept.impact: Denial of Service on CI resources.

kept.title: Use of 'ts-ignore' in Security Critical Logic
kept.description: The use of @ts-ignore when handling IPv6 mapping signals an attempt to suppress type-checking for logic that is likely brittle and dangerous.
steps_to_exploit: Pass unexpected input to IPv6 parsing logic
Typescript fails to flag invalid property access
Application crashes or enters an undefined state
kept.impact: Reduced security posture due to silent failure handling.

kept.title: Sensitive Information Disclosure via Debug Logging
kept.description: The is_url_safe_debug function logs full URLs, which might contain authentication tokens or PII, to the console output.
steps_to_exploit: Call the debug function with a credentialed URL
View server logs
Extract credentials from logs

kept.title: Missing Input Sanitization for IP Converters
kept.description: Methods like bin_ip_to_normal_ip rely heavily on regex but do not strictly handle potential overflows or edge cases in numeric base conversions.
steps_to_exploit: Submit extremely long binary strings
Cause parsing errors or unexpected logic flow
Possible memory issues or incorrect IP validation
kept.impact: Logic error leading to bypass of IP-based validation.

kept.title: Weak Error Handling in Redirect Logic
kept.description: The is_redirect_safe function returns false (safe) for catch blocks, which might accidentally swallow critical errors or bypass checks if a URL is malformed in a specific way.
steps_to_exploit: Submit a specifically malformed URL that triggers a URL constructor error
The code returns 'false' (safe) instead of 'error'
Downstream processes might trust the 'false' return value
kept.impact: Security logic bypass due to masking failures.

kept.title: Insecure Permissions on Pull Request Actions
kept.description: The workflow uses pull_request_target on untrusted code; even with limited permissions, this exposes the workflow to potential injection if any input is used unsafely.
steps_to_exploit: Attacker submits a PR with a malicious branch name or metadata
The workflow processes the PR, potentially exposing the CI context

kept.title: Lack of Strict Input Validation for Octal IPs
kept.description: The octal converter allows octal strings which are common vectors for SSRF (e.g., 0177.0.0.1 being interpreted as 127.0.0.1).
steps_to_exploit: Inject an octal-encoded IP address
The regex passes, and conversion logic transforms it into a bypass-friendly loopback address
kept.impact: Successful SSRF using obfuscated IP notation.

kept.title: Inconsistent Normalization Order
kept.description: is_url_safe performs Unicode normalization, then backslash replacement, then slash normalization. This order of operations can be manipulated to hide bypass characters.
steps_to_exploit: Use character sequences that normalize into separators after string replacements
Bypass the URL parser security checks
kept.impact: Security checks are performed on strings that don't match the final interpreted URL.
